tag: the stage goes back to being a literal on the blocking path
why: The committed defect, restored at the writer M1 found it at. It is one word and it is printed by three readers beside a status of 'body pending' whose own basis names four sections still awaiting the owned model.

tag: only one of the two establish paths derives the stage
why: THE EXACT SHAPE THAT PRODUCED THIS ROW. W496 derived the status on both paths and the stage on neither; a round that fixed one establish path and not the other would leave the SSE path stamping a literal, and the blocking path's green would hide it. The leg counts derivation sites per module rather than naming line numbers.

tag: a section composed out of order carries the entity past an earlier one
why: `break` -> `continue` turns the contiguous prefix into 'the last one composed', so a commercialisation written while the concept is still pending reports the entity as commercialised. That is this row's own defect one section along, and it is a one-word change that still reads like a loop over the lifecycle.

tag: a missing body map reads as nothing composed
old:
return (None, "no body-pending map is recorded on this entity, so which §4 sections it has "
                      "composed is NOT KNOWN - which is not the same as having composed none, and "
                      "not the same as having composed them all")
why: NOT KNOWN collapsed into a measured zero. The stage is still None so every other assertion passes; only a leg that checks the BASIS distinguishes 'we looked and nothing is composed' from 'there is nothing to look at'. A measured zero is a finding; an unmeasured one is not.

tag: the shipped README prints the raw field again
why: A writer fixed without its readers moves the untruth down a layer - and this reader writes to DISK, into a repository the founder keeps after the page that would have explained it is gone. With the literal removed this prints the word None, which reads as a bug rather than as a state.

tag: a placeholder counts as a composed strategic layer
why: The committed defect: truthiness. Every basis string survives this edit, so a guard checking the WORDING still passes - the `if False and` shape that made four blinds vacuous two rounds ago. The leg drives the placeholder through the function and reads `holds` back.

The subtlest restoration available: `holds` is still computed correctly and still rendered, so the page shows 'placeholder' while layers_present counts the layer. A reader comparing the chip with the list would see the contradiction; a guard that only checked `holds` would not.

tag: a board roster is an action plan again
why: This layer's own basis has said since W496 that a roster is not a plan of action and no action items are recorded. The pack contradicted itself one key apart for 77 rounds, and the half that travelled was the wrong one.

tag: the per-layer state stops reaching the page
why: A renamed key is silent in JavaScript: the page maps over undefined, renders no chips and throws nothing. The basis would again be reachable only through the chip that appears when a layer is MISSING - so the one thing that could reveal a wrong count would once more be gated behind the count being wrong.

tag: Operate is ticked by a repository existing
why: The committed defect: 'Run · defend · improve · grow' ticked because files were written. The hint still reads correctly off the living roster in this state, so the tile would say it is not operating AND show a tick - which is how a half-fix looks.

tag: the §4 rail goes back to one flag for six stages
old:
const st = railState(key, result);
            const done = st.done;
new:
const st = railState(key, result);
            const done = !!result;
why: The nastiest of this set: railState is still called and the per-stage chip still renders 'not run', while the TILE lights as complete. The page would state both things at once, and a guard that only checked the chips would pass.

tag: a stage the journey never reached counts as done
old: if (v.ran === false) return { done: false, label: 'not run',
new: if (v.ran === true) return { done: false, label: 'not run',
why: `ran` is present and FALSE only for a stage that never ran, and ABSENT on a complete journey - so testing for `=== true` matches nothing and every blocked stage falls through to 'ran'. The contract is easy to invert because absent-means-ran is the opposite of the usual reading, which is why it is measured in the comment above it.

tag: a stage with no verification borrows another's
old: if (!v) return { done: false, label: 'not known',
why: NOT KNOWN promoted to a pass, which is the three-state failure this programme keeps finding: a stage the journey recorded nothing about is reported as verified. Model · Simulate · Rank has no verification entry at all, so this is a live path and not a hypothetical.

tag: the cockpit renders nothing when no stage is reached
why: Silence is not honesty. An absent badge leaves a reader unable to tell 'no stage reached' from a field that failed to load, and the original code was exactly this shape - `{detail.stage && <Badge>}` - which is why removing the literal alone would not have been a fix.
